title: How Kenyans Abroad Can Send Money Home Cheaply
excerpt: Comparing transfer fees, exchange rates, and delivery speed across the services Kenyans in the diaspora use most.

content: For most Kenyans in the diaspora, sending money home isn't a one-time event, it's a recurring part of life, whether that's supporting parents, paying school fees, or helping with a family project. Because it happens so often, even a small difference in fees or exchange rates adds up fast over a year. Here's how to think about the main options.

Transfer fees and exchange rate markups can quietly eat 3 to 8 percent of every remittance, depending on the provider and the payment method you use. That markup is often hidden inside the exchange rate itself rather than shown as a separate fee, which makes it easy to underestimate how much you're actually paying. Two providers advertising the same flat fee can still cost very differently once you account for the rate they use to convert dollars to shillings.

publish their fees upfront and use the real mid-market exchange rate, which usually makes them cheaper for bank-to-M-Pesa transfers than a traditional wire from a US bank. The tradeoff is that transfers can take a bit longer to land compared to services built specifically for instant cash pickup.

is worth comparing too, especially for cash pickup in areas without reliable mobile money access, or when you need funds to arrive within minutes rather than a day. Its network of physical agent locations across Kenya is one of its biggest advantages, even if the exchange rate isn't always the most competitive.

A traditional international wire from a US bank is usually the slowest and most expensive route, often layering a flat fee on top of a weaker exchange rate, plus a possible receiving fee on the Kenyan side. Services that deposit directly into M-Pesa tend to be faster and cheaper for smaller, more frequent transfers, since the money is usable almost immediately without a trip to a bank branch.

body.text: Tips to Cut Costs Every Time

content: Compare the total amount the recipient actually gets, not just the advertised fee, since that's the only number that reflects the real exchange rate markup. Sending larger amounts less frequently, rather than many small transfers, also reduces how much you lose to flat fees over time.
